intent: The verified customer wants the 28 Sep £2,525 Oakfield Direct Debit stopped, refunds of the 24 Aug and 23 Sep £875 collections, and a refund of the 24 Sep £6.50 unarranged overdraft fee.
summary: ID&V passed. At the customer's request, ask Direct Debit operations to cancel the Oakfield mandate OPM-78COOMBE-3312 and stop the £2,525 collection due 28 Sep if it can still be stopped. Log a Direct Debit Guarantee claim for both £875 collections so they can be assessed. Register a complaint about the £6.50 fee. Ask whether Oakfield sent advance notices. Tell the customer all of this is pending: there is no promise that Monday's collection will be stopped or that any refund will be paid.

facts.claim: The customer passed ID&V on the personal banking phone line.

The account is a personal current account with no arranged overdraft. The active monthly Direct Debit mandate is H&V COLLECT / OAKFIELD PM (since Feb 2025), ref OPM-78COOMBE-3312, SUN H&V COLLECT 771902.
£875.00 was collected on 24 Aug 2026 and £875.00 on 23 Sep 2026 under mandate OPM-78COOMBE-3312.
The 23 Sep collection took the balance to -£412.90. A £6.50 unarranged overdraft daily fee was applied on 24 Sep, taking the balance to -£419.40.
A £2,525.00 collection with narrative 'FINAL ACCOUNT 78 COOMBE RD' is scheduled for 28 Sep 2026. The bank received the instruction on 24 Sep 2026 at 02:10:44Z and its status is 'scheduled'.
A £1,019.40 transfer from savings posted on 25 Sep and the available balance is now £600.00.
In an email dated 1 Sep 2026, Oakfield confirmed that the tenancy at 78 Coombe Road ended on 31 Aug 2026. It said the check-out report would follow and the deposit would be dealt with after that.
The bank cannot see whether Oakfield sent advance notices for the September collections.

The customer says the agency told her the collection was 'already submitted' and could not be cancelled on their side. She wants both £875 collections refunded, Monday's collection stopped and the fee refunded.

missing: Whether the 28 Sep £2,525 collection can still be stopped once the mandate is cancelled (the instruction is already with the bank)
Whether Oakfield sent advance notices for the 23 Sep and 28 Sep collections, and when
Which rent period each £875 collection covered (the 24 Aug collection fell before the 31 Aug tenancy end)
What the £2,525 'final account' is made up of (the check-out report and deposit were still pending at 1 Sep)
The outcome of the Guarantee claim assessment and of the fee complaint

steps.instruction: At the verified customer's request, cancel Direct Debit mandate OPM-78COOMBE-3312 (originator Oakfield Property Management Ltd, SUN H&V COLLECT 771902, payer account SYN-SC-05-1 / SYN-ACCT-05-1). Stop the scheduled £2,525.00 collection dated 28 Sep 2026 ('FINAL ACCOUNT 78 COOMBE RD', instruction received 24 Sep 2026 02:10:44Z) if it can still be stopped. Report back whether the mandate is cancelled and whether the 28 Sep collection was stopped or remains in process.

rationale.explanation: The customer, who passed ID&V, asked for Monday's collection to be stopped after her tenancy ended on 31 Aug. The instruction is already with the bank and marked scheduled, so whether it can be stopped has to be confirmed rather than assumed.
rationale.criterion: A verified payer may cancel a Direct Debit at the bank. Collections already in process may not be stoppable, so cancellation must not be promised.

steps.target: Direct Debit operations (Harrow & Vale Bank plc)

steps.instruction: Log a Direct Debit Guarantee claim for Gabriela Petrova on mandate OPM-78COOMBE-3312 covering: (a) £875.00 collected 23 Sep 2026, after Oakfield's written confirmation (email of 1 Sep 2026) that the tenancy ended on 31 Aug 2026, with advance notice status unknown to the bank; and (b) £875.00 collected 24 Aug 2026, which the customer also disputes and which was collected before the tenancy end date. Attach the agency email, the statement extract and the 24 Sep instruction record. Ask the team to assess both items under the Guarantee's error criteria, including advance notice and whether each collection was properly due, and to record the outcome.

rationale.explanation: The customer asks for refunds of both collections. The 23 Sep one came after the confirmed tenancy end and advance notice is unknown. The 24 Aug one came during the tenancy, and no error is evident from the records so far. Both should be assessed rather than decided here.
rationale.criterion: The Guarantee covers errors in Direct Debit set-up or collection. It must be kept separate from cancelling future collections, and a refund must not be promised for every dispute with a supplier.

steps.target: Direct Debit Guarantee / indemnity claims team

steps.instruction: Register a complaint from Gabriela Petrova about the £6.50 unarranged overdraft fee applied on 24 Sep 2026. The fee followed the 23 Sep £875 Oakfield collection, which took the balance to -£412.90 on an account with no arranged overdraft. The customer says it was not her fault and wants the fee refunded. Note the related Guarantee claim (s2) and the request to stop the 28 Sep collection (s1). Record her wider dissatisfaction that she wants all the Oakfield collections refunded.

rationale.explanation: The customer is unhappy with a bank fee and wants it refunded, which is a complaint seeking redress. It should be handled separately from the Direct Debit work.
rationale.criterion: Register the complaint as its own piece of work alongside the operational query. Do not promise redress before review.

steps.instruction: Ask: 'Did Oakfield send you any advance notice of the £875 taken on 23 September or the £2,525 due on 28 September? If so, when did you get it, and could you send us a copy?'

rationale.explanation: The bank cannot see whether advance notices were sent. This fact matters for assessing the Guarantee claim.
rationale.criterion: Ask the customer for the specific missing fact that affects the decision.

steps.instruction: Say: 'I'm asking our Direct Debit team to cancel the Oakfield Direct Debit and to stop Monday's £2,525 payment if it can still be stopped. The instruction reached us on 24 September, so I can't promise it will be stopped yet, and we'll confirm what happens. If it does go out, it would be more than the £600 you have available. Cancelling the Direct Debit doesn't settle whatever Oakfield says is owed on the final account, so any disagreement about that amount is with Oakfield. I'm logging both £875 payments for review under the Direct Debit Guarantee. That covers mistakes in a collection, like a wrong amount or date or no advance notice. The September one came after your tenancy ended, and the August one came before it ended. I can't tell you yet whether either will be refunded. I'm also registering a complaint about the £6.50 overdraft fee. Its outcome isn't decided yet, and we'll update you.'

rationale.explanation: The customer needs to know what is being done for each of her four requests and that none of the outcomes is confirmed yet.
rationale.criterion: Reply with the current status and say clearly what it does not confirm. Do not promise completion or outcomes.

must_state: The mandate cancellation and the attempt to stop Monday's £2,525 collection have been requested but are not yet confirmed. The instruction was received on 24 Sep and stopping it is not guaranteed.
Cancelling the Direct Debit does not settle or cancel any amount Oakfield says she owes. Any dispute about the 'final account' is between her and Oakfield.

Both £875 collections are being logged as a Direct Debit Guarantee claim for assessment. The Guarantee covers errors in a collection, such as a wrong amount, wrong date or missing advance notice. A refund depends on that assessment.
Her complaint about the £6.50 overdraft fee is being registered and its outcome is not yet known.
If the £2,525 collection does go out, it would be more than her £600 available balance.
must_not: Do not promise that the 28 Sep collection will be stopped
Do not promise or confirm a refund of either £875 collection or of the £6.50 fee
Do not state that Oakfield failed to send advance notice; the bank cannot see this
Do not state that cancelling the mandate ends any debt to Oakfield
Do not say any requested team action has been completed
Do not give a fixed response deadline or promise a callback time
